release-scale-matrix-unmeasured.observation: The required 21/32/64/100 release scales have not been measured; this host runs only the separate 4-validator minimum-BFT functional tier.
release-scale-matrix-unmeasured.reason: The available measurement server is a 6-core KVM guest with 11.68 GiB RAM. Co-locating 21 validators would reserve about 8.0 GiB for the N5 pending-finality budget alone and would not represent the one-validator-per-host topology required by section 0.5.
release-scale-matrix-unmeasured.closure_condition: Run every required release scale with one validator per reviewed host or VM at the exact N5-complete measured commit and retain the manifests and results.

carrier-scale-transport-unmeasured.observation: No cluster run has transported a finality carrier near the 984260-byte 400-signer ceiling over the reviewed 100 Mbps symmetric deployment link.
carrier-scale-transport-unmeasured.reason: The 4-validator functional tier carries only an approximately ten-kilobyte certificate and therefore cannot exercise the carrier, admission-pool, fan-out or network-capacity ceilings.
carrier-scale-transport-unmeasured.closure_condition: Run the live overlay scenario at a signer count that produces a carrier near the 984260-byte ceiling on the reviewed deployment network and retain separate payload, queueing, propagation and verification evidence.

sustained-finality-distribution-unmeasur.observation: No N6 cluster run reports a sustained-operation distribution of persisted-finality latency; the scale sweep records one first proposal/notarization/FinalCert sequence per cold start.
sustained-finality-distribution-unmeasur.reason: Repeated cold starts produce repeated first-event observations, not many finality-latency samples inside steady-state operation, so they cannot establish the p99 quantity used by max_p99_persisted_finality_ms.
sustained-finality-distribution-unmeasur.closure_condition: After a declared warmup, observe and correlate many production finality events through persistence during one sustained run, retain the per-event monotonic latency samples, and report a distribution with enough samples to support its claimed percentile rather than a first-event timestamp.
